Terminals: DRL-Based Joint Terminal Scheduling
and UAV 3D Trajectory Design
Yunfei Gao , Graduate Student Member, IEEE, Xiaopeng Yuan , Member, IEEE,
Dingcheng Yang , Member, IEEE, Yulin Hu , Senior Member, IEEE, Yue Cao , Senior Member, IEEE,
and Anke Schmeink , Senior Member, IEEE
Abstract—In this paper, we investigate an unmanned aerial ve-
hicle (UAV)-assisted edge computing network in a sophisticated
three-dimensional (3D) scenario, e.g., a post-disaster urban area
with multiple mobile ground terminals (GTs) for resilience. The
mission of the UAV is to first collect a set of computation tasks from
multiple GT sources, then process them and make joint decisions
(computation results) which are finally transmitted to another set
of GT destinations. An efficient design is provided aiming at min-
imizing the total time cost including costs for the task offloading,
computations, and decision transmissions, via jointly designing the
UAV’s trajectory and the scheduling of communications from and
to different GTs. In particular, we take into account the practical
assumptions on the GTs’ mobility, on the obstacle avoidance to 3D
buildings, and on that the UAV is possible to fly among buildings,
i.e., the flying altitude can be lower than the buildings’ heights. To
address the established complex and non-convex problem, we first
provide a problem transformation by exploiting Markov decision
process (MDP), and then propose a deep reinforcement learning
(DRL) approach-based solution with a multi-step dueling DDQN
(D3QN) method. As a result, an efficient solution is achieved, where
the UAV acts as the agent to continuously explore and improve
its mobile strategy during interacting with the environment under
the proposed method. The simulation results show the advantages
of the proposed 3D trajectory design in comparison to a 2D one.
In addition, the results confirm the robustness of the proposed
design in terms of different GTs’ mobility models and UAV flying
height/area limits, and illustrate the superiority of unrestricted
feasible domains for the UAV flight.

the UAV trajectory and resource allocation. Furthermore, with
the rapid development of the machine learning (ML) industry,
a set of ML-based trajectory designs have been provided for
UAV-assisted wireless networks, e.g., authors in [15] introduce a
deep reinforcement learning (DRL) based approach to minimize
the UAV mission completion time by jointly optimizing the
UAV’s trajectory and the association between UAV and ground
base stations, while a semi-distributed resource management
approach is proposed in [16] to minimize the system’s sum

The above trajectory design works [9], [10], [11], [12], [13],
[14], [15], [16] are conducted under the assumptions of a simpli-
fied LoS-dominant channel model and a two-dimensional (2D)
trajectory, i.e., the UAV flies at a fixed altitude. In fact, via
enjoying the freedom of flying altitude, a 3D trajectory design is
expected to achieve a higher performance in comparison to a 2D
one. In particular, an efficient design of UAV’s 3D trajectory also
faces two significant challenges. On the one hand, optimizing
a 3D trajectory requires a simultaneous consideration of the
UAV’s motion in both horizontal and vertical directions, which
leads to a significantly high complexity in comparison to a 2D
case. On the other hand, the 3D trajectory is restricted more by
the detailed characteristics of the environment, which requires
the design to carefully take into consideration environmental
factors such as altitude variation, multi-dimensional propagation
characteristics, and the effects of obstacles and blockages on the
channel. Hence, for a UAV-assisted multi-GT MEC network, it
is essential to take the practical probabilistic LoS channel states
into account.
Under a practical probabilistic LoS channel model, the au-
thors in [17], propose a UAV-assisted multi-GT framework by
optimizing the 3D UAV trajectory to maximize the minimum
(average) expected rate among GTs. The authors of [18] provide
a 3D trajectory design method for harvesting solar energy and
collecting data from multiple smart GTs. In addition, the works

design the UAV’s 3D trajectory to enhance the data collection
performance. Moreover, the works of [21], [22], [23] enhance the
communication performance of the UAV as a mobile MEC node
by optimizing its 3D trajectory. However, the aforementioned
have the assumption that GTs are fixed, i.e., the mobility of GTs
is ignored. It is worth noting that the GTs may be in a mobile
state under a practical scenario leading to that the mobility of
GTs cannot be ignored. Furthermore, the above works [12], [13],
under the assumption that the UAV is flying over buildings,
without considering the case of low-altitude flying of the UAV,1
and thus ignoring the UAV’s obstacle avoidance issue, which
usually results in a challenging problem. However, in certain

we consider a UAV-enabled MEC scenario with more practical
assumptions, e.g., with respect to the mobility of GTs, feasible
UAV flying zones amidst buildings, obstacle avoidance in a 3D
environment, and the utilization of a probabilistic LoS channel
for communication with the 3D buildings. In the considered

Assuming that all GTs are moving at all times and that the
UAV can fly between buildings (under obstacle avoidance con-
straints), we aim at minimizing the whole operation time cost
via joint determining the 3D trajectory and the communication
schedule from and to different GTs. The formulated problem
is non-convex and difficult to solve the dynamic environment
caused by the mobility of GTs, i.e., being intractable via ap-

matching theory). In addition, compared to 2D trajectory design,
the expanded exploration space of 3D trajectory design results
in slower convergence of the algorithm. Consequently, it is
essential to design algorithms that accelerate convergence and
enhance overall performance. To solve such issues, we provide a
joint design based on a modified reinforcement learning (RL) al-
gorithm, i.e., the UAV acts as an agent acquiring the information
of GTs in the process of interacting with the environment, learns
the underlying model of the GTs’ random moving behavior
(through continual interaction learning between the agent and
the environment), and adjusts its trajectory accordingly. The

VI. CONCLUSION
In this paper, we considered a UAV-assisted MEC network
with multiple mobile GTs and probabilistic LoS channels. We
provided a design minimizing the whole operation time via
jointly optimizing the UAV 3D trajectory together with the
scheduling of offloading transmissions from source GTs and
decision transmissions to destination GTs. In particular, an
unrestricted feasible domain for the UAV flight is adopted in the
design while obstacle avoidance to the 3D building is guaran-
teed. To address the problem, we first transform the established
problem into an MDP and then propose a D3QN-based method
in which the UAV acts as an agent to explore and learn the
policy of 3D trajectory and scheduling GTs. Via simulations,
the convergence of the proposed method is confirmed, and
appropriate hyperparameters of the proposed method are also
investigated. In addition, we investigated the performance of
the proposed method in terms of operation time and robustness,
as well as the impacts on the system setups, e.g., GTs’ moving
model, UAV flying altitude, on the designed 3D trajectory, and
scheduled results.
We finalize the whole paper by spotlighting its high exten-
sibility. On the one hand, this paper is the first endeavor to
propose a joint optimization of 3D UAV trajectory and GTs’
communication scheduling by taking into account various prac-
tical aspects of the scenarios, including 3D buildings obstacle
avoidance, GTs with mobile capability, and feasible UAV flying
zone among buildings. Through simulation experiments, it was
discovered that the proposed method has a strong robustness
performance under different setups with respect to different GTs
mobility behavior scenarios, different initial conditions, various
UAV flying altitude ranges, and trajectory designs in different
dimensions. In addition, allowing UAV to fly at a low altitude
can significantly reduce mission completion time. Furthermore,
compared to 2D trajectory design, the performance improve-
ment achieved with 3D trajectory design is mainly attributed
to its increased design freedom in both transmission distance
and elevation angles. Moreover, the proposed method can be
extended to other system designs, e.g., joint resource allocation
involving transmitting bandwidth and computation frequency,
designs that allow GTs to fly, multi-UAV joint trajectory designs,
other practical channels, etc. On the other hand, in order to
solve the joint optimization problem, a modified DDQN, i.e., the
D3QN method is introduced, which accelerated the convergence
speed and improved the stability of the method. The proposed
D3QN method is expected to facilitate the designs for scenarios
having non-convex and complicated constraints and difficulties
achieving convergence.

VI. CONCLUSION
In this paper, we considered a UAV-assisted MEC network
with multiple mobile GTs and probabilistic LoS channels. We
provided a design minimizing the whole operation time via
jointly optimizing the UAV 3D trajectory together with the
scheduling of offloading transmissions from source GTs and
decision transmissions to destination GTs. In particular, an
unrestricted feasible domain for the UAV flight is adopted in the
design while obstacle avoidance to the 3D building is guaran-
teed. To address the problem, we first transform the established
problem into an MDP and then propose a D3QN-based method
in which the UAV acts as an agent to explore and learn the
policy of 3D trajectory and scheduling GTs. Via simulations,
the convergence of the proposed method is confirmed, and
appropriate hyperparameters of the proposed method are also
investigated. In addition, we investigated the performance of
the proposed method in terms of operation time and robustness,
as well as the impacts on the system setups, e.g., GTs’ moving
model, UAV flying altitude, on the designed 3D trajectory, and
scheduled results.
We finalize the whole paper by spotlighting its high exten-
sibility. On the one hand, this paper is the first endeavor to
propose a joint optimization of 3D UAV trajectory and GTs’
communication scheduling by taking into account various prac-
tical aspects of the scenarios, including 3D buildings obstacle
avoidance, GTs with mobile capability, and feasible UAV flying
zone among buildings. Through simulation experiments, it was
discovered that the proposed method has a strong robustness
performance under different setups with respect to different GTs
mobility behavior scenarios, different initial conditions, various
UAV flying altitude ranges, and trajectory designs in different
dimensions. In addition, allowing UAV to fly at a low altitude
can significantly reduce mission completion time. Furthermore,
compared to 2D trajectory design, the performance improve-
ment achieved with 3D trajectory design is mainly attributed
to its increased design freedom in both transmission distance
and elevation angles. Moreover, the proposed method can be
extended to other system designs, e.g., joint resource allocation
involving transmitting bandwidth and computation frequency,
designs that allow GTs to fly, multi-UAV joint trajectory designs,
other practical channels, etc. On the other hand, in order to
solve the joint optimization problem, a modified DDQN, i.e., the
D3QN method is introduced, which accelerated the convergence
speed and improved the stability of the method. The proposed
D3QN method is expected to facilitate the designs for scenarios
having non-convex and complicated constraints and difficulties
achieving convergence.
